gestalt: A valley of giants standing in moss. On the Hoh's terraces Sitka spruce and western hemlock rise 75-80 m, widely spaced, over a floor that is more than half moss and carpeted with sword fern and oxalis rather than brush, because the elk eat the brush. Every fallen tree becomes a nursery: nearly all young trees stand on logs, so the living forest grows in rows, on stilts and arches of root. Bigleaf maple groves carry more living epiphyte than leaf, their limbs fat with moss and hung with clubmoss streamers that glow yellow-green when the light comes through. The light is soft, green and wet; fog sits in the valley in the mornings. Beside it all runs the river, milky slate blue from the glaciers of Mount Olympus, braided over wide grey bars piled with whole drift trees, alder on the older bars, the valley walls rising into cloud.
